title: OpenAI president: Companies need to do 10 things now for cybersecurity
excerpt: "Time is of the essence," OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman said while sounding the alarm that companies need to upgrade their cybersecurity efforts.
content_html:
OpenAI president says companies should do 10 things ASAP to defend against AI cyber threats

By Brent D. Griffiths

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

OpenAI's president is ringing the cybersecurity alarm bell.

Greg Brockman says companies need to act now to secure their systems against AI-powered attackers after the "watershed moment for cybersecurity" that was the OpenAI-Hugging Face hack.

"I've spoken with many organizations over the past few weeks, and one theme is clear: they know they need to fundamentally uplevel their cybersecurity practices with unprecedented speed," the OpenAI president and cofounder wrote in a post on his personal blog published on Monday morning.

Brockman said AI tools will soon be able to find vulnerabilities as OpenAI's models did when they breached Hugging Face's systems. At the same time, the OpenAI cofounder wrote, "AI will also make it much easier" to fix those flaws to prevent hacks.

'Pursue the steps below at turbo speed'

OpenAI disclosed in July that, during internal testing, its AI agents were able to break out of a testing environment and then later compromise Hugging Face, a platform where developers publish, share, and download AI models.

The incident underscores how important preparing against vulnerabilities, Brockman wrote.

Brockman shared a 10-point list of actions companies, or "defenders," should take as soon as possible to bolster their cybersecurity. "Time is of the essence, and defenders will need to pursue the steps below at turbo speed."

  1. Get organizational commitment and buy-in.
  2. Give your security team an agent.
  3. Equip that agent with security expertise.
  4. Run security assessments against your own systems immediately.
  5. Work through your existing vulnerability backlog.
  6. Put security review directly into your development process.
  7. Have the agent help fix what it finds.
  8. Incrementally automate detection triage.
  9. Have an AI-assisted forensic investigation capability ready before you need it.
  10. Experiment, run hack weeks, and iterate rapidly.


"The defender's window is open now," Brockman wrote. "Over the coming months, every organization will need to begin significantly automating its security program to stay secure, and the security community must urgently rise to define the tools, practices, and playbooks that will increase the power of defenders faster than that of attackers as AI continues to advance."

OpenAI 总裁表示公司应尽快采取 10 件事来防御人工智能网络威胁

布伦特·D. Griffiths 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

OpenAI 总裁敲响了网络安全警钟。

格雷格·布罗克曼 (Greg Brockman) 表示，在 OpenAI-Hugging Face 黑客事件这一“网络安全的分水岭时刻”之后，公司需要立即采取行动，保护其系统免受人工智能攻击。

这位 OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人在周一上午发表的个人博客上发表的一篇文章中写道：“过去几周我与许多组织进行了交谈，有一个主题很明确：他们知道需要以前所未有的速度从根本上提升其网络安全实践。”

布罗克曼表示，人工智能工具很快就能发现漏洞，就像 OpenAI 的模型在破坏 Hugging Face 系统时所做的那样。 与此同时，这位 OpenAI 联合创始人写道，“人工智能也将使修复这些缺陷以防止黑客攻击变得更加容易”。

“以极快的速度执行以下步骤”

OpenAI 在 7 月份透露，在内部测试期间，其 AI 代理能够突破测试环境，随后又入侵 Hugging Face（开发者发布、共享和下载 AI 模型的平台）。

布罗克曼写道，这一事件凸显了针对漏洞做好准备的重要性。

布罗克曼分享了公司或“捍卫者”应尽快采取的 10 点行动清单，以加强其网络安全。 “时间至关重要，防守者需要以极快的速度执行以下步骤。”

  1. 获得组织的承诺和支持。
  2. 为您的安全团队指定一名代理。
  3. 为该代理配备安全专业知识。
  4. 立即针对您自己的系统运行安全评估。
  5. 处理现有的漏洞积压工作。
  6. 将安全审查直接纳入您的开发流程。
  7. 让代理帮助修复其发现的问题。
  8. 逐步自动化检测分类。
  9. 在需要之前准备好人工智能辅助的取证调查能力。
  10. 进行试验、运行黑客周并快速迭代。

“防守者的窗户现在打开了，”布罗克曼写道。 “在接下来的几个月里，每个组织都需要开始显着自动化其安全计划以确保安全，安全社区必须紧急定义工具、实践和手册，随着人工智能的不断发展，这些工具、实践和手册将比攻击者更快地增强防御者的力量。”
